# Functions

Functions are called from expressions (05 §4.7, §12). A random one draws from the rule stream and is refused in a pure context; one that is not *safe for belief* is refused in a mind context, where a character decides by what it has perceived (05 §7.3). Functions mods define are listed in their own files, not here.

## Combat

<a id="contest"></a>
### `contest`

`contest(contest: id<contest>, a: real, b: real) -> real?` · safe for belief · random

A margin of a contest (07 §4.1): the scaled difference, or log-ratio, of `a` and `b`, plus logistic noise of the contest's spread drawn from the rule stream. At or above zero, `a` won. Refused in a pure context. Null for a value that is null.

- `contest` (id<contest>): The contest.
- `a` (real): The value of the side the margin favours when it is positive.
- `b` (real): The value of the other side.

<a id="odds"></a>
### `odds`

`odds(contest: id<contest>, a: real, b: real) -> real?` · safe for belief

The chance that a margin of a contest is at or above zero (07 §4.1), from 0 to 1. Pure: it draws nothing. Null for a value that is null.

- `contest` (id<contest>): The contest.
- `a` (real): The value of the side the margin favours.
- `b` (real): The value of the other side.

## Data

<a id="has-def"></a>
### `has_def`

`has_def(type: string, id: string) -> bool` · safe for belief

Whether a definition of a type with a qualified id is loaded.

- `type` (string): The definition type: `material`, `block`.
- `id` (string): The qualified id.

<a id="setting"></a>
### `setting`

`setting(id: string) -> any` · safe for belief

The value of a setting (04 §10), or null if it has none.

- `id` (string): The setting's qualified id.

## Lists, maps and text

<a id="cap"></a>
### `cap`

`cap(text: string) -> string` · safe for belief

The text with a capital first letter.

- `text` (string): A text.

<a id="contains"></a>
### `contains`

`contains(xs: any, x: any) -> bool` · safe for belief

Whether a list has an element equal to `x`, or a text contains `x`.

- `xs` (any): A list or a text.
- `x` (any): An element to find in a list, or a text in a text.

<a id="first"></a>
### `first`

`first(xs: list<any>) -> any` · safe for belief

The first element of a list. Null for an empty list.

- `xs` (list<any>): A list.

<a id="has"></a>
### `has`

`has(m: map<any>, key: any) -> bool` · safe for belief

Whether a map has an entry for a key.

- `m` (map<any>): A map.
- `key` (any): A text or an id.

<a id="keys"></a>
### `keys`

`keys(m: map<any>) -> list<string>` · safe for belief

The keys of a map, in order of key.

- `m` (map<any>): A map.

<a id="last"></a>
### `last`

`last(xs: list<any>) -> any` · safe for belief

The last element of a list. Null for an empty list.

- `xs` (list<any>): A list.

<a id="len"></a>
### `len`

`len(x: any) -> int` · safe for belief

The number of elements of a list, entries of a map or characters of a text.

- `x` (any): A list, a map or a text.

<a id="str"></a>
### `str`

`str(x: any) -> string` · safe for belief

The value as text: a number as written, an id as its qualified id, `null` for null.

- `x` (any): Any value.

<a id="sum"></a>
### `sum`

`sum(xs: list<number>) -> number` · safe for belief

The total of a list of numbers. An int if all are ints. Zero for an empty list.

- `xs` (list<number>): A list of numbers.

<a id="values"></a>
### `values`

`values(m: map<any>) -> list<any>` · safe for belief

The values of a map, in order of key.

- `m` (map<any>): A map.

<a id="without"></a>
### `without`

`without(xs: list<any>, x: any) -> list<any>` · safe for belief

A copy of a list without the elements equal to `x`.

<a id="without-key"></a>
### `without_key`

`without_key(m: map<any>, key: any) -> map<any>` · safe for belief

## Maths

<a id="abs"></a>
### `abs`

`abs(x: number) -> number` · safe for belief

The magnitude of `x`, of the same type as `x`.

- `x` (number): A number.

<a id="atan2"></a>
### `atan2`

`atan2(y: real, x: real) -> real` · safe for belief

The angle in radians, from -pi to pi, of the point (x, y) measured from the positive x axis.

- `y` (real): The point's y.
- `x` (real): The point's x.

<a id="ceil"></a>
### `ceil`

`ceil(x: number) -> int` · safe for belief

The smallest int that is not less than `x`.

- `x` (number): A number.

<a id="clamp"></a>
### `clamp`

`clamp(x: number, low: number, high: number) -> number` · safe for belief

`x` limited to the range from `low` to `high`. If `low` is greater than `high` the result is `high`. An int if all three are ints.

- `x` (number): The number to limit.
- `low` (number): The least it may be.
- `high` (number): The most it may be.

<a id="cos"></a>
### `cos`

`cos(x: real) -> real` · safe for belief

The cosine of an angle.

- `x` (real): An angle in radians.

<a id="div"></a>
### `div`

`div(a: int, b: int) -> int` · safe for belief

Integer division, rounding toward minus infinity, so that `div(a, b) * b + a % b == a`. Null, with a warning, when `b` is zero.

- `a` (int): The dividend.
- `b` (int): The divisor.

<a id="exp"></a>
### `exp`

`exp(x: real) -> real` · safe for belief

`e` raised to the power `x`.

- `x` (real): The power.

<a id="floor"></a>
### `floor`

`floor(x: number) -> int` · safe for belief

The largest int that is not greater than `x`.

- `x` (number): A number.

<a id="lerp"></a>
### `lerp`

`lerp(a: real, b: real, t: real) -> real` · safe for belief

`a + (b - a) * t`: the value `t` of the way from `a` to `b`.

- `a` (real): The value at `t` = 0.
- `b` (real): The value at `t` = 1.
- `t` (real): How far from `a` to `b`. Not limited to 0..1.

<a id="ln"></a>
### `ln`

`ln(x: real) -> real` · safe for belief

The natural logarithm. Null, with a warning, for zero or less.

- `x` (real): A positive number.

<a id="log10"></a>
### `log10`

`log10(x: real) -> real` · safe for belief

The base-10 logarithm. Null, with a warning, for zero or less.

- `x` (real): A positive number.

<a id="max"></a>
### `max`

`max(a: number, b: number...) -> number` · safe for belief

The largest of its arguments. An int if all are ints, otherwise a real.

- `a` (number): A number.
- `b` (number): Another number; more may follow.

<a id="min"></a>
### `min`

`min(a: number, b: number...) -> number` · safe for belief

The smallest of its arguments. An int if all are ints, otherwise a real.

- `a` (number): A number.
- `b` (number): Another number; more may follow.

<a id="round"></a>
### `round`

`round(x: number) -> int` · safe for belief

The nearest int to `x`. Halves round away from zero.

- `x` (number): A number.

<a id="sign"></a>
### `sign`

`sign(x: number) -> int` · safe for belief

`1` for a positive number, `-1` for a negative one, `0` for zero.

- `x` (number): A number.

<a id="sin"></a>
### `sin`

`sin(x: real) -> real` · safe for belief

The sine of an angle.

- `x` (real): An angle in radians.

<a id="sqrt"></a>
### `sqrt`

`sqrt(x: real) -> real` · safe for belief

The square root. Null, with a warning, for a negative number.

- `x` (real): A number that is not negative.

## Perception

<a id="could-perceive"></a>
### `could_perceive`

`could_perceive(a: entity, at: any, kind: string) -> bool?` · not in a mind context

Whether a signal of a kind at a place would reach `a` now through one of its senses (15 §6). Null for a place, an entity or a kind that names nothing.

- `a` (entity): Who would perceive.
- `at` (any): A cell, or something that is somewhere.
- `kind` (string): The signal kind's id, qualified or bare.

<a id="perceives"></a>
### `perceives`

`perceives(a: entity, b: entity) -> bool?` · not in a mind context · reactive

Whether `a` has `b` detected now (15 §6). Null if either is not an entity. Window kinds use `perceives(self, source)` as their `noticed_if`.

- `a` (entity): Who perceives.
- `b` (entity): Whom or what.

Its result changes on `detected`, `lost_track`.

## Random

<a id="chance"></a>
### `chance`

`chance(p: real) -> bool` · safe for belief · random

True with probability `p`. Zero or less is never; one or more is always.

- `p` (real): A probability from 0 to 1.

<a id="pick"></a>
### `pick`

`pick(list: list<any>) -> any` · safe for belief · random

One element of a list, each equally likely. Null for an empty list.

- `list` (list<any>): The list to choose from.

<a id="rand"></a>
### `rand`

`rand(a: real, b: real) -> real` · safe for belief · random

A random real from `a` up to but not including `b`.

- `a` (real): The least the result may be.
- `b` (real): The result is less than this.

<a id="rand-int"></a>
### `rand_int`

`rand_int(a: int, b: int) -> int` · safe for belief · random

A random int from `a` to `b`, both included. `a` if `b` is less than `a`.

- `a` (int): The least the result may be.
- `b` (int): The most the result may be.

## Space

<a id="dir"></a>
### `dir`

`dir(from: any, to: any) -> list<int>?` · safe for belief · reactive

The step from one thing toward another: the signs of the shortest offset east, south and up, each -1, 0 or 1. Null where `dist` is null.

- `from` (any): Where the step starts.
- `to` (any): What it is toward.

Its result changes on `entity_relocated`.

<a id="dist"></a>
### `dist`

`dist(a: any, b: any) -> real?` · safe for belief · reactive

The distance between two things in metres, a storey counting three, the shorter way round on wrapped axes (02 §3.3). Each is a cell, an element, or something that is somewhere: an entity, an area (its middle), a site (its anchor). Null if either is nowhere or they are in different grids.

- `a` (any): One end.
- `b` (any): The other end.

Its result changes on `entity_relocated`.

<a id="light"></a>
### `light`

`light(at: any) -> real?` · not in a mind context

How bright a cell is now (15 §3.3). The same as its `light` property.

- `at` (any): A cell, or something that is somewhere.

<a id="los"></a>
### `los`

`los(a: any, b: any) -> bool?` · not in a mind context · reactive

Whether terrain leaves a clear line between two things, each as for `dist`, an entity seen from and at the height it stands at (02 §22). Null if either is nowhere, or the line comes to space that is not loaded before anything blocks it.

- `a` (any): One end.
- `b` (any): The other end.

Its result changes on `entity_relocated`, `element_changed`.

<a id="offset"></a>
### `offset`

`offset(at: loc, dx: int, dy: int, dz?: int) -> loc?` · safe for belief

The cell so many cells east, south and up of a cell, wrapped on wrapped axes. Null beyond an edge of the realm.

- `at` (loc): The cell to start from.
- `dx` (int): Cells east.
- `dy` (int): Cells south.
- `dz` (int, optional): Storeys up. Zero if left out.

## Text for a reader

<a id="a"></a>
### `a`

`a(x: any) -> string` · safe for belief

What the reader calls `x`, with an indefinite article where one belongs.

- `x` (any): A subject, or anything a reader can be shown.

<a id="count"></a>
### `count`

`count(n: number, word: string) -> string` · safe for belief

A number with its noun: "3 arrows", "1 arrow".

- `n` (number): How many.
- `word` (string): The noun in the singular.

<a id="list"></a>
### `list`

`list(xs: list<any>) -> string` · safe for belief

A list written out: "a knife, a rope and two coins".

- `xs` (list<any>): The things to list.

<a id="name"></a>
### `name`

`name(x: any) -> string` · safe for belief

What the reader calls `x`: "you" for the reader, a known name, or a description of what the reader made out.

- `x` (any): A subject, or anything a reader can be shown.

<a id="plural"></a>
### `plural`

`plural(word: string) -> string` · safe for belief

The plural of a noun.

- `word` (string): The noun in the singular.

<a id="the"></a>
### `the`

`the(x: any) -> string` · safe for belief

What the reader calls `x`, with a definite article where one belongs.

- `x` (any): A subject, or anything a reader can be shown.

<a id="their"></a>
### `their`

`their(x: any) -> string` · safe for belief

The possessive for `x`; "your" for the reader.

- `x` (any): A subject, or anything a reader can be shown.

<a id="them"></a>
### `them`

`them(x: any) -> string` · safe for belief

The object pronoun for `x`; "you" for the reader.

- `x` (any): A subject, or anything a reader can be shown.

<a id="themself"></a>
### `themself`

`themself(x: any) -> string` · safe for belief

The reflexive pronoun for `x`; "yourself" for the reader.

- `x` (any): A subject, or anything a reader can be shown.

<a id="they"></a>
### `they`

`they(x: any) -> string` · safe for belief

The subject pronoun for `x`; "you" for the reader.

- `x` (any): A subject, or anything a reader can be shown.

<a id="verb"></a>
### `verb`

`verb(x: any, word: string) -> string` · safe for belief

The verb agreeing with `x`: "you hit", "the guard hits".

- `x` (any): A subject, or anything a reader can be shown.
- `word` (string): The verb in its plain form: 'hit'.

## Time

<a id="local-now"></a>
### `local_now`

`local_now(subject: any) -> real?` · not in a mind context

The local time of the clock a subject is on, in seconds (03 §3.4): an entity's clock, the clock of a cell, an area's or a realm's own. Null for a subject on no clock.

- `subject` (any): What to read the clock of.

<a id="now"></a>
### `now`

`now() -> real` · safe for belief

Universal time, in seconds since the simulation began.

## Types

<a id="exists"></a>
### `exists`

`exists(x: any) -> bool` · not in a mind context

Whether what a reference points at still exists.

- `x` (any): A reference to a subject.

<a id="is-null"></a>
### `is_null`

`is_null(x: any) -> bool` · safe for belief

Whether a value is null.

- `x` (any): Any value.

## Windows

<a id="away-from"></a>
### `away_from`

`away_from(who: any, from: any) -> string?` · safe for belief

The step that leads straight away from `from` for `who`: `north`, `north_east`, `east`, `south_east`, `south`, `south_west`, `west` or `north_west`, by the signs of the shortest offset on the level. Null for two in one column, or either nowhere. What a reaction that leaves steps by (07 §5.2). Safe for belief, as `dir` is.

- `who` (any): Who steps: an entity or a cell.
- `from` (any): What it steps away from: an entity or a cell.

<a id="window-kind-of"></a>
### `window_kind_of`

`window_kind_of(window: window?) -> id<window_kind>?` · safe for belief

The kind of a window that is still open.

- `window` (window?): The window.

<a id="window-open"></a>
### `window_open`

`window_open(window: window?) -> bool` · safe for belief

Whether a window is still open (03 §7.1).

- `window` (window?): The window.

<a id="window-source"></a>
### `window_source`

`window_source(window: window?) -> entity?` · safe for belief

Whose action or rule opened a window that is still open; null for one that is closed or has no source. Safe for belief: a window is offered only to those who perceive its source (03 §7.2).

- `window` (window?): The window.

<a id="window-time-left"></a>
### `window_time_left`

`window_time_left(window: window?, who: entity) -> real?` · not in a mind context

Seconds of `who`'s own time before a window is expected to close: when the phase that opened it ends, where that phase leads straight to the one that closes it, or when its length is over. Null for a window that is closed or whose deadline is not known.

- `window` (window?): The window.
- `who` (entity): Whose own time it is counted in.
